limits.source: own cap of 9,000 below the 10,000 calls per account and day in Govee's v1 API PDF; the v2 reference (get-you-devices, 'Friendly Reminder', 2026-07-06) names per-minute limits per device and account but no daily one — kept by the rate limiter over a sliding day that outlives a restart (rate-limiter.ts)
own cap of 20 below the 30 per account and minute of Govee's v2 reference (get-you-devices, 'Friendly Reminder', 2026-07-06) — kept by the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts)

own cap of 20 below the 30 per device and minute of Govee's v2 reference (get-you-devices, 'Friendly Reminder', 2026-07-06; state, scenes and DIY scenes alike) — kept by the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts)

Govee's v2 reference (get-you-devices, 'Friendly Reminder', 2026-07-06): 2 per second and device, burst 6 — as a window the burst of six, then two a second on average (6 in any 3 s stay within 6 + 2 per second) — kept by the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts)

Govee's v2 reference (get-you-devices, 'Friendly Reminder', 2026-07-06): 12 per second and account, burst 80 — as a window the burst of 80, then twelve a second on average (80 in any 7 s stay within 80 + 12 per second) — kept by the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts)
own cap of the adapter — Govee documents none for this undocumented app endpoint: one call a second on average; every request waits at the call gate (call-gate.ts) until it fits

own cap of the adapter — Govee documents none: the libraries, SKU features and snapshot packets of every light keep a small lane of their own, so an undocumented endpoint is never stormed and no command waits for them — kept by the rate limiter (rate-limiter.ts)
own cap of the adapter — the Govee app version is looked up once per adapter start and once a day; a restart right after a start makes two within a minute, the call gate (call-gate.ts) holds a third

own cap of the adapter — Govee documents none for its events broker: one connection a minute; reconnecting-mqtt-client opens one only while this window and the write window have room, and the window outlives a restart (limit-memory.ts)

own cap of the adapter — Govee documents none: a connection writes CONNECT and SUBSCRIBE, then a ping every 60 s (keepalive); every packet counts as it leaves (mqtt.js packetsend), and a SUBSCRIBE or a ping waits for room (reconnecting-mqtt-client) — the window stays under half the keepalive, so a ping held back is still answered in time

counterparts.name: Govee account broker connection (AWS IoT MQTT)

limits.source: own cap of the adapter below AWS IoT Core's 1 CONNECT per second and client id (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/iot-core.html, read 2026-11-10): two connections a minute; reconnecting-mqtt-client opens one only while this window and the write window have room, and the window outlives a restart (limit-memory.ts)

own cap of the adapter far below AWS IoT Core's 100 publish requests per second and connection, beyond which publishes are discarded (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/iot-core.html, read 2026-11-10): CONNECT, SUBSCRIBE, the 60 s ping, every command and status request (K18) count as they leave (mqtt.js packetsend); a command or status request goes out only while the window has room and is refused otherwise (govee-mqtt-client), a SUBSCRIBE or a ping waits for room (reconnecting-mqtt-client)
own cap of the adapter — one scan datagram per target every 30 s plus the scan at start; the scan skips a target that would go over it (govee-lan-client)
own cap of the adapter — Govee's LAN API documents none; the LAN client delays a datagram that would go over it (govee-lan-client)
